summary: The optional cli_auth rollout corrections are coherent for the reviewed branch, but newly published dependencies invalidate three frozen assumptions: Identity is now a single transactional auth.sqlite3 authority, ADR-0028 is already assigned to that accepted decision, and origin/main now has six required runtime-flag rows. These are technical architecture corrections and require no product decision.

findings.description: The frozen plan still designs device grants as JSON sidecars coordinated with sessions by a process/file lock. The newly published shared-auth dependency establishes one transactional auth.sqlite3 Identity authority, and its accepted ADR explicitly rejects sidecar Identity stores and cross-store recovery. Its SessionRepository is now an AuthStore facade carrying auth_version, auth_method, and provider_binding_id. Implementing the frozen design would split grant consumption, source-session validation, and session issuance across authorities. The rollout also lacks an explicit prerequisite that the modern-auth migration and a SQLite-capable rollback image are established before the CLI candidate; without that order, its claim that the predecessor is safe for an initial rollback can be false after the Identity epoch changes.

findings.recommendation: Rebase the architecture on the published Identity authority before implementation. Store device authorization state inside AuthStore and consume it in the same transaction as fresh account/auth_version/source-session checks and CLI session issuance; reuse the existing opaque-cookie wire contract and do not introduce a JSON grant authority or filesystem authorization lock. Add an explicit dependency gate requiring the modern-auth release/import and a verified auth.sqlite3-capable rollback floor before the CLI release, or fully specify the combined migration and its forward-repair-only failure path. Update the data model, device contract, tasks, purge/export plan, concurrency tests, and rollout contract accordingly.

findings.description: The CLI package proposes a second ADR-0028 and requires acceptance by the ambiguous shorthand ADR0028, while the published shared-auth dependency already contains an accepted ADR-0028 governing the same Identity boundary. Merging both leaves two different decisions with the same number and makes plan, task, rollout, and review references non-deterministic.

findings.recommendation: After rebasing against the published decisions, assign the CLI authorization amendment the next unused ADR number and make it amend the accepted modern Identity ADR as well as ADR-0019 where applicable. Update every plan/task/contract reference and regenerate the reviewed ADR digest binding before the next frozen review.

findings.description: The corrected optional-row strategy is sound in principle, including missing cli_auth resolving OFF without insertion and preserving absence through seed, upgrade, read, unrelated mutation, scrub, and metadata writes. Its frozen factual baseline is now stale: origin/main has six required rows after adding task_mcp, while the plan, rollout contract, and proposed ADR still specify five. Because the repository validates an exact managed-row set and upgrades older inventories explicitly, implementing the five-row design can omit task_mcp or degrade the store. A later generic reconciliation task does not make the currently reviewed migration contract accurate.

findings.recommendation: Update the frozen artifacts to six required rows plus optional cli_auth. Preserve task_mcp and all six existing cohorts through every seed, marker/ledger write, upgrade, read, unrelated mutation, scrub, and reconstruction path; only an explicit cli_auth operator mutation may insert the optional seventh row. Add tests starting from current six-row stores as well as historical upgrade shapes, then update the proposed ADR digest and rerun the frozen campaign.
